shipped_change.nature: generic term-level synonyms; triggers are single terms or catalog phrases, none taken from eval question wording; no per-query branch

rejected_revision.why: first revision matched phrases taken from the tuned questions themselves; test-set leakage

questions.q: how do we ship a change to only five percent of traffic and watch it
we lost a namespace and need the data restored
our kubernetes spend is growing faster than usage
several teams want to share one gpu node
alerts wake me up but most are noise
proving the artifact we run was built from our source
restricting pod to pod traffic in a shared cluster
isolating ai generated code so it cannot reach production

leg_ablation_under_rejected_rules.note: measured before the rules were made generic; retained to show the both-legs requirement, not as current numbers

latency_ms.method: 36 sequential warm queries per mode (12 tuned questions x3), port-forwarded single-node cluster

limitations: Both sets are small and hand-judged with 1-4 relevant ids per query; the result bounds the claim to these judged paraphrases.
The tuned set was read while the rules were written (in-sample); the 8-question held-out set, written by the same author after the rule table existed, is the primary evidence.
Keyword mode improves too, so hybrid-versus-keyword narrows; the change is query understanding, not a hybrid-only fix.
One measurement session against a single-node cluster; no longitudinal or live-traffic A/B data.

harness_run.note: judged sets imported from side-effect-free scripts/search-eval-set.ts; earlier runs imported search-eval.ts, whose top-level main() started the full eval concurrently

superseded_revision.why: generic synonyms but four triggers were still eval-question phrases; removed
